trust_decision.summary: Whether a peer-supplied packet length (header length field) plus header/offset fits in a signed int before it sizes the TCP receive buffer; decided in packet_get_length's remain block and in tcp_expand_buffer.

landing_point.why: Summary names the inet TCP driver receive buffer; tcp_expand_buffer computes ulen = used + len and sizes/reallocs the receive buffer.

fix_sites.entry_point: gen_tcp sockets with {packet, 1|2|4|sunrm|asn1|cdr|fcgi|tpkt|ssl_tls} via inet_drv tcp_remain (inet_drv.c:12709), and erlang:decode_packet/3 BIF (erl_bif_port.c:1556), which gen_tcp_socket (inet_backend=socket) uses (lib/kernel/src/gen_tcp_socket.erl:2478-2502)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared lower-level packet parser in the VM core (erts/emulator/beam), not in the driver

fix_sites.entry_point: gen_tcp receive (active delivery and gen_tcp:recv) via tcp_recv/tcp_deliver -> tcp_remain -> tcp_expand_buffer (inet_drv.c:12724, 12748, 12897)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: erts/emulator/beam/packet_parser.c:483-491 (shared packet_get_length, also behind erlang:decode_packet/3 at erts/emulator/beam/erl_bif_port.c:1556)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report says the overflow is in the inet TCP driver's receive buffer, and packet_get_length already has a 'wrap-around protection' check (packet_parser.c:486-487), so a solver may guard only tcp_expand_buffer and treat the VM-core parser as correct; for the O8 route, packet_size is set by the trusted local application, not the peer.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: packet_size=0 means 'no limit': legitimately large length-prefixed packets (and gen_tcp:recv(S,N) up to 64 MB, inet_drv.c:12118) must still be accepted and the buffer grown; the in-buffer 'virtual size' shrink path must keep working. Also TPKT/SSLv2 header-minus-constant underflows must still yield an error, not a packet.

O6_input_shapes: asn1 long-length form up to 4 bytes (packet_parser.c:342-354)
packet_size unset (0) vs set (max_plen branch, packet_parser.c:486)
header offset 'used' > 0 inside an existing buffer (inet_drv.c:11467)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: tcp_remain line-mode/unknown-length branch passes the unsigned packet_size option to tcp_expand_buffer as int; a packet_size above INT_MAX becomes a negative len, which the fix's 'len > INT_MAX - used' guard does not reject, and the returned read size is psize - n
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: packet_size is local configuration (prim_inet type uint, erts/preloaded/src/prim_inet.erl:1758,1946) rather than peer input, and values above 2 GB look like a misconfiguration
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as landing point, ~1300 lines away; option parsing in erts/preloaded/src/prim_inet.erl

O8b_injection_room.sibling: tcp_push_buffer allocates desc->i_bufsz + len in int without an overflow check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same int buffer-size arithmetic style as tcp_expand_buffer; a maintainer adding a size-sum here would plausibly skip the guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: decode_packet/3 accepts packet_size up to UINT_MAX and passes it as max_plen to packet_get_length
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A clamp to INT_MAX at the option boundary is a natural place for a planted missing check, at distance from the driver.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: SCTP fragment buffer growth already has an explicit INT_MAX headroom check; a planted copy without it fits the existing idiom
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Shows the maintainers' own overflow idiom next to an analogous buffer-growth path.

O9_family: integer overflow (signed int length/offset sum) leading to heap buffer overflow (CWE-190 -> CWE-122)

O10_build.toolchain: autoconf ./otp_build / configure && make; gcc, perl, ncurses; no Docker needed in principle

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an INT_MAX check on used + len in tcp_expand_buffer only, leaving packet_get_length's remain sum (and its reliance on tlen < hlen) unchanged.

out_of_scope_notes: SSL/TLS framing in lib/ssl is done in Erlang; not reviewed.
packet_size uint option has no upper bound in prim_inet (erts/preloaded/src/prim_inet.erl:1946); its encoding to int32 is not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured; OTP is a large tree (likely hundreds of MB), so giant/tiny flags were not set.

Whether the published packet_parser change, which drops the 'tlen < (int)hlen' wrap check (fix.diff:76-91), still rejects plen near UINT_MAX when a caller sets max_plen > INT_MAX - hlen (decode_packet/3 allows up to UINT_MAX, erl_bif_port.c:1527). This matters for hidden-test fairness.
Exact peer-controlled value range that reaches sock_recv with an oversized nread at the pinned commit was reasoned from code, not run.
Recall risk is estimated; how widely the advisory is written up was not checked (no network).
